subtopic: Schedule II and III quantity limits
stem: While reviewing the prescription, a Massachusetts pharmacy reviews a new Depo-Testosterone prescription. Select all conclusions supported by the canonical rules.

choices.text: On this record, a qualifying non-opioid Schedule III prescription may use the statutory 90-day single-fill pathway for testosterone cypionate.
For this scenario, covered dispensing is reportable to MassPAT for testosterone cypionate.
Under these facts, federal Schedule III refill limits remain a separate check when refills are authorized for testosterone cypionate.
In this setting, the drug is Schedule VI because it is a hormone for testosterone cypionate.
The original can be refilled without regard to federal refill limits for testosterone cypionate.

related_facts: testosterone cypionate (Depo-Testosterone) is used for replacement therapy in males with conditions associated with deficient endogenous testosterone; it is federal Schedule III and Massachusetts Schedule III.

Massachusetts generally limits Schedule II and III opioid prescriptions to a 30-day supply and recognizes defined 90-day pathways for OUD drugs, non-opioid Schedule II or III drugs, and implantable infusion pumps.

Covered pharmacies report dispensing of Schedule II through V controlled substances and DPH-designated additional drugs, including gabapentin, to the Massachusetts PMP under the current submission standard.
